status: GAME BALANCE. Tunable gameplay values for simcore/engagement.hpp. These are not performance data for any real system; only the values whose 'source' names a document come from one, and those only set when lamps light.
notes: Change these to tune difficulty. The debrief prints every factor that went into each hit or miss, so the effect of a change is visible.

zone.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p15 (zone at 300 m/s: 1500-10300 m, 25-5000 m), p121 and p129 (ВНИМАНИЕ at least 15 s before the meeting point enters the zone; eq. 2.24); SAM Simulator Osa-AK manual p9, p14, p29 agrees.
zone.notes: The kill zone, judged at the meeting point (engagement.hpp, LaunchZoneFor): ЦЕЛЬ В ЗОНЕ lights while a missile launched now would meet the target inside it. ВНИМАНИЕ lights for an approaching target within max_range_m + (max_range_m / missile average speed + warning_s) x its speed over the ground (10.3 km + 36 s x V).

zones.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p15 (head-on at 300 m/s: 25-5000 m, 1.5-10.3 km, crossing parameter to 6 km; at 500 m/s: 100-5000 m, 1.5-10 km, parameter to 4 km; helicopters hovering or to 100 m/s on the TV: 10-25 m, 2-6.5 km), p124-128 (the fire-control computer's zone: slant parameter <= 8700 - 8 V, eq. 2.18; a receding meeting point <= 8700 - 8 V, eq. 2.19), p257 (Table 7.1: the far edge of the launch zone head-on, by height, up to 300 m/s and faster; 25-50 m, 100, 150, 200-5000 m). flak11 (the same bands; pursuit to 6.5 km, 100-5000 m, up to 300 m/s), mon_2112_80 p10-12 (parameter 6 / 4 km), korovin_tiv_2010 (6 km); docs/research/OSA_RESEARCH_2026-10.md section 5, OSA_MANUALS_2026-10.md.
zones.notes: Each band is judged at the meeting point (engagement.hpp, MeetingFor: the target straight on, the missile along the line of sight at its average speed). The crossing parameter is how far the target's course passes from the unit, over the ground; the slant parameter adds its height. A meeting point still approaching is head-on, otherwise pursuit; the pursuit edge is 8700 m less 8 m per m/s (7.1 km at 200 m/s; flak11's flat 6.5 km is close at 275 m/s). launch_range_m is the crews' Table 7.1 (the target's range at launch, linear between the heights, flat beyond): the computer's own speed functions (eqs. 2.17, 2.20, 2.23) are not printed, and the table carries their effect on low and fast targets (8 km at 25-50 m against 16 km at altitude). The inner limits after the crossing point (eqs. 2.21-2.22) are not modelled.

tv.source: reticle_deg: ePap (samsim_thread): the TV sight is tracked by hand with a 3-mil reticle, 3 thousandths on the 6000-division circle = 0.18 degrees; memory_s follows ePap's memory mode (it carries on at the last angular rates when the target is masked). Range judged from the target's size in the reticle: ePap (samsim_thread), by the artillery formula of the thousandth (range = size x 1000 / thousandths). span_m are PLACEHOLDER sizes typical of each class (a scenario target can give its own span_m); size_error (0.15 of the span, one sigma, one judgement per target) and size_min_mils (0.3 thousandths: a tenth of the reticle) are estimates. The rest are game values.
tv.notes: Manual TV tracking. The TV channel follows the wheels: the target has to stay in the lens field (data/procedures/osa_ak.json, sensors.track.fov_deg) around where the azimuth and elevation wheels point, or the track is lost. An NPC in a wheel's seat follows the target npc_delay_s behind it and no faster than the aim rates; the player turns the wheels. The mean distance of the target from the crosshair during a missile's flight costs hit chance: factor = max(error_factor_min, 1 - error_penalty_per_reticle x mean error / reticle). Without this group the servo drives the wheels onto the target by itself once the TV has locked.

methods.source: samsim_thread (creator, ePap: T/T above elevation 00-30, the 'Gorka' zoom climb or 'F' for low targets); korovin_tiv_2010 (Gorka against targets at 50-100 m, so the fuse is not set off by the ground).
methods.notes: 00-30 is 30 thousandths on the Soviet 6000-division circle: 1.8 degrees. The method is printed in the debrief and decides nothing else: its effect is in outcome.low_altitude. 'N' (ПОМЕХА on: against a jammer, or with no range) has its own outcome factor (outcome.method_factor).

search.notes: Game value: with СДЦ (MTI) off, targets below this height are lost in ground clutter.

track.source: range_gate_m: half the 1.5 km magnified sweep, SAM Simulator Osa-AK manual p24. The rest are game values; clutter_altitude_m rests on the SSC range channel sharing the MTI canceller (mon_2112_80 p15, p23) and is an estimate.
track.notes: How close the operator must set the azimuth line and range gate for ЦУ АЗ to capture; below min_altitude_m the radar can't hold angles (НЛЦ) and the TV must be used; below clutter_altitude_m it can't hold the target in the ground clutter unless the operator has СДЦ on (ssc.mti). em_capture_*: with the EM layer the auto-capture circuit takes the lock once the tracking radar has echoed on 22 of its last 40 looks (4 s; a local Pd of about 0.55). A raw lock starts on a lucky echo far out where Swerling I detection is still a few tenths (27 km for a 3 m2 target at 5 km altitude); this rule is tied to the one fitted calibration (Korovin's 23 km at 5 km altitude, Pd 0.5): it captures that target at 21 to 25 km. Raising the Pd does not help his 14 km at 50 m (the full-path Pd of a 50 m target is smooth: 0.5 at 22 km, 0.8 at 18 km). A model choice, not a published figure.

arm.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p263, Table 7.3 (read from the page image: the range to the target when the tracking transmitter's high voltage goes on, for the missile to meet it at the near / far edge of the zone; target speed over 300 m/s: 9 / 24 km, under 300 m/s: 7 / 20 km)
arm.notes: Firing under the threat of anti-radiation missiles (p262): the tracking transmitter radiates only from these ranges. The NPC commander uses the far-edge column (scenario doctrine arm_threat); the target's speed is what the senior operator's scope shows.

aim.notes: Roles: who turns each wheel (flak11, 9A33-3); they are console stations. The rest are game values: how fast an NPC turns each wheel onto a contact. plotting_board_range_m: the crew acts on a designation from the PU-12 within 50 km (manual p21 watches the board from there; the board itself is in the battery's post and the vehicle has only the designations it heard, flak11). tv_search_*: with the radars silent the crew search for a designated target with the TV, sweeping 15 degrees each side of the designation and stepping the elevation a field height up and down (3 bars); a designation read out on the battery net can be a minute old. Game values (sam3d estimate), not a published drill.

missile.source: average_speed_mps: voenizdat_osa_1991 p129 (21 s of flight to the zone's far edge, 10.3 km: 490 m/s); max_flight_time_s: voenizdat_osa_1991 p22, p180 (self-destruct at 25-28 s), p177 (maximum flight 24-27 s); SAM Simulator Osa-AK manual p27 (24-27 s).
missile.notes: Not a flight model: the missile flies along the line of sight at its average speed to where it meets the target flying straight on, and the result comes then. A meeting later than max_flight_time_s is out of reach (the missile destroys itself).

outcome.source: method_factor and no_range_fuse_factor follow samsim_osa p34 and samsim_thread (ПОМЕХА selects method N and arms the fuse at once, with the medium beam, because there is no range to arm it by); voenizdat_osa_1991 p23-24 (fuse arming against a jamming target); the numbers are game values. low_altitude is calibrated to the published single-missile kill probabilities (docs/research/OSA_RESEARCH_2026-10.md section 5): flak11 (strike aircraft at 10 m 0.12-0.55, helicopters at 10 m 0.07-0.12, cruise missiles at 10 m 0.12-0.38) and korovin_tiv_2010 (0.35-0.4 at 50 m, 0.42-0.85 above 100 m, original 9K33 against an F-4C). With the class chances above this gives a fighter 0.39 at 50 m, a bomber 0.32 and a helicopter 0.10 at 10 m. Everything else here is a game value.
outcome.notes: Game values. chance = hit_chance[class] x (TV track ? tv_factor : 1) x (in zone at launch ? 1 : outside_zone_factor) x max(manoeuvre_factor_min, 1 - penalty x target turn rate in deg/s) x max(deviation_factor_min, 1 - deviation_penalty x crew mistakes) x low_altitude[class](height of the target above the ground at impact), linear between the points, flat beyond them x method_factor[guidance method] (N: three-point on angles alone, the fuse armed early: a guess at 0.75) x (no range at launch and ПОМЕХА off ? no_range_fuse_factor : 1): with no range and ПОМЕХА off the fuse, armed by range, never arms.

kill_assessment.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p267 (the result observed to decide on engaging again or ceasing fire; the fullest picture on the TV in good visibility, otherwise the range indicator and the synchro dials; the signs of a hit and of a miss); scope_gone_s: a turn of the search antenna at 33 rpm, voenizdat_osa_1991 p24, and a little; every number here is a sam3d estimate.
kill_assessment.notes: Game values for simcore/kill_assessment.hpp. Each sign weighs for a hit (> 0) or a miss (< 0); signs adding up to 'decisive' settle the call, made no sooner than judge_min_s after the meeting; otherwise the judge (judge_role, or the commander) calls it by their sum at judge_max_s, wrong with ambiguous_wrong_chance plus his tier's branch_error_chance, and 'not observed' with no sign at all. Of the outcome model's misses by chance, near_burst_chance burst beside the target (the burst and the reply gone, as for a hit) and early_burst_chance before the meeting; the rest pass by (the reply goes on). A destroyed aircraft leaves the instruments at once (its mark gone, read from them); its fall on the elevation dial (elevation_drop_chance), fire on the TV (tv_fire_chance) and its group, jamming and chaff signs are drawn at delay_s after the meeting. A live target's elevation falling faster than elevation_drop_deg_s reads as a fall. strobe_match_deg and beside_m say which strobe, group and chaff echoes are the target's. A target called destroyed and still on the search scope recheck_s later: the senior operator says it flies on.

group.source: voenizdat_osa_1991 p261 (a target in a group the senior commander's radars can't resolve is designated by the group's centre and a selection rule: the first to fourth from the left of the nearest targets, on one azimuth by range; with no rule the crew chief chooses); same_azimuth_deg: the search radar's azimuth beam, 1.3 +- 0.4 deg, voenizdat_osa_1991 p24; post_unresolved_m: the PU-12M's errors of up to 3 km (flak11) taken as the distance below which its picture can't tell two aircraft apart, a sam3d reading; search_m and link_m are sam3d estimates (search_m as the designation search, simcore/scenario_runner.hpp kDesignationSearchM).
group.notes: simcore/group_designation.hpp. The post designates by centre and rule when the mark it gives has other hostile marks within post_unresolved_m (linked). The crew takes the echo nearest the centre within search_m and the echoes linked to it within link_m as the group, counts them from the left as it looks at them (on one azimuth: within same_azimuth_deg, by range) and takes the rule's; a rule beyond the group's size takes the last.
